extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners handling patent litigation (equity practice) in U.S. federal courts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on procedural discovery, bills of particulars, interrogatories, counterclaims, and equitable defenses in patent infringement suits in equity courts. Covers what must or may be disclosed, limits on interrogatories, and when equity jurisdiction exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interchange of dates of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice (Southern District of New York) obliges each party to inform the other of the respective dates of invention they intend to prove: the plaintiff must inform the date of invention of the patent in suit, and the defendant must inform the date(s) of invention of any inventions by which he expects to anticipate the plaintiff's invention. The interchange is required to be simultaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to narrow issues; simultaneous disclosure recommended in jurisdictions following this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in bill of particulars for prior use/invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill of particulars of the answer will not be required to state in whose presence an alleged prior use or invention occurred, but the defendant will be required to give a description of the thing or things invented or used or the ingredients of a composition or manufacture or of a process involved or practiced in its production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant may refuse to disclose a secret process; requirements apply when the process is set up as an anticipation; interrogatories may be more appropriate if the purpose is to ascertain the nature of an infringing article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to name patents/publications used as anticipations
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts (Southern District of New York practice) have required the defendant to name the patents and publications that will be offered in evidence to support the contention of anticipation, and among those, to declare which of them the defendant will rely on at trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Learned Hand noted that while a defendant may plead many patents, a court may direct the defendant to limit the number of patents he 'seriously contends to be anticipations.' Sanctions (costs) may be used where defendant could reasonably have cut down the patents relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion and jurisdictional variation on requiring specification of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Some courts (e.g., Northern District of Ohio) have taken a contrary view and held that such a bill of particulars may be absolutely required, while other courts limit such requirements and may impose only costs as sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should check local practice; inability to comply with an absolute listing may preclude evidentiary use of unlisted items but may also preclude imposition of full penalties in some courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: patents/publications as anticipations vs as evidence of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When patents and publications are used as anticipations they are the things themselves (ultimate facts) to be proved; but when used merely to show the prior state of the art they are evidence and a court should not compel disclosure of the evidence that an opponent will use to establish the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bill of particulars is more appropriate for identifying ultimate facts; compelling production of evidence (even limited to patents/publications) is outside the purpose/functions of a bill of particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of persons having prior knowledge or prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: The names of those having prior knowledge or having made prior use of an invention in suit should be required on the same terms and conditions as a statement of anticipating patents and publications; but the names of witnesses to the prior knowledge or use should not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between identifying the actor(s) who had prior knowledge/use (may be required) and requiring lists of witnesses (generally not required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explain how pleaded patents disclose elements or negative novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: In some courts (Northern District of Ohio) a bill of particulars will be required of the defendant setting forth in what respects each of the patents pleaded in the answer discloses any of the elements or combinations of elements described in the patent in suit, and in what respect they negative the novelty and invention of the device shown and described in the complainant's letters patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operates to force mapping of prior patents to claim elements; tensions exist between this requirement and the traditional function of pleadings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff's duty to identify alleged points of infringement (but not element-by-element mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill of particulars will not generally be granted compelling a plaintiff to point out in what particular part of an alleged infringing machine each element of the patent in suit is embodied, although a plaintiff probably would be required to advise the defendant what parts of the defendant's machine are infringed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interrogatories or requests for inspection/production to discover details about alleged infringing structure rather than demanding element-by-element mapping in a bill of particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and scope of specific interrogatories under Equity Rule 58
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific interrogatories have been retained as a separate procedure: the defendant may use interrogatories to sustain his defence as the plaintiff formerly could to sustain his bill; interrogatories permit discovery of facts and documents material to the support or defence of the cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatories are directed to facts/documents material to the party's own claims/defences and are not intended to enable a party to discover the evidence or witnesses the opponent will use solely to establish the opponent's case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories limited to facts/material documents supporting own claim or defence
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the present rules, interrogatories are intended to allow discovery only of such facts and documents as will sustain the claims of the party filing the interrogatories (or his defence), not to ascertain matters relating exclusively to the opponent's title or ground of defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts reject interrogatories that would force a party to disclose his 'case' or matters having no relation to the interrogating party's ground of action or defence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to provide evidentiary opinions or comparisons in interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories requiring opinions (e.g., as to reading of contracts, functions of machinery) or comparisons that are evidentiary in character (e.g., comparisons between blueprints) are objectionable because they ask for evidence or expert opinion rather than ultimate facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the documents themselves are the best evidence, require production/inspection of originals rather than compelling narrative descriptions or opinion-based comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interrogatories requesting contents of documents the proponent can produce
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories inquiring as to the contents of documents which it is within the power of the proponent of the interrogatories to produce are objectionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek production rather than a narrative recital when originals or copies are within opponent's control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule against 'fishing expeditions' and undue burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories intended merely to 'ascertain the opponent's case' or that impose unreasonable burdens are improper; discovery should be permitted only where facts are difficult to procure by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will deny discovery that is inquisitorial, unwarranted, or unnecessary because the facts can be otherwise procured; avoid broad, speculative queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories to corporate officers and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If any party is a corporation, an opposite party may apply for an order allowing him to file interrogatories to be answered by any officer of the corporation, and an order may be made for the examination of such officer upon such interrogatories as the court shall think fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision relieves the necessity of joining corporate officers as parties when only discovery (not substantive relief) is sought; practice varies on whether interrogatories may be directed to the corporation without a prior order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity discovery limitation where suit may impose penalties (treble damages)
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been held that discovery will not be allowed in suits in which a penalty may be inflicted on the offender; accordingly an interrogatory asking whether the defendant had practiced the patented process was held objectionable in a patent infringement suit because the defendant may be held liable for treble damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of precedents holding that equitable discovery may be restricted where civil penalties or punitive-like remedies are possible; arguments differ among courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of counterclaims under Rule 30 (Equity Rule 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 30 the defendant may set forth any counterclaim arising out of the transaction which is the subject-matter of the suit, and may set out any set-off or counterclaim which might be the subject of an independent suit in equity against the plaintiff; counterclaims for infringement by the plaintiff of patents relating to the same subject-matter, and counterclaims for unfair competition involving respective patent rights, have been held proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A counterclaim must generally arise out of the same subject-matter; if the counterclaim's federal jurisdiction turns on diversity, requisite diversity must exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional limits on counterclaims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a counterclaim is cognizable in federal court by reason of the subject-matter (e.g., patent infringement) it is proper even though the court might not have acquired original jurisdiction for an independent suit; but if jurisdiction of the counterclaim would rest only on diversity (e.g., unfair competition) there is no jurisdiction unless the requisite diversity exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a counterclaim may waive objections to personal jurisdiction; verify jurisdictional basis before asserting or resisting a counterclaim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences available in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The twenty-eight defences which may be made to actions at law for infringements of patents may all be made to actions in equity; in addition, equity suits are also liable to two other defences not available at law: non-jurisdiction of equity, and laches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatise recommends explaining facts supporting each defence and appropriate pleading forms; counsel should consider how these defences operate differently in equity than at law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable jurisdiction prerequisites in patent suits (non-jurisdiction of equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equity jurisdiction is absent where the patent expired before the bill is filed, or where the complainant has no ownership in the patent at the time the bill was filed; equitable title arising out of an executory contract to assign is insufficient to confer jurisdiction. Equity jurisdiction exists where an injunction is rightfully prayed for or where legal remedies are inadequate, difficult, or incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bill filed before patent expiration and a proper injunction is sought, equity should retain jurisdiction even if the patent later expires or other changes occur; allegations must state a proper case for injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity jurisdiction where patents are combined and damages cannot be apportioned
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill for infringement of both an expired and an unexpired patent states grounds for equitable relief where the defendant has combined the devices of both patents in a single machine so conjoined that it is practically impossible to apportion the damages and profits between the two patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity may retain jurisdiction in cases involving multiple patents tied together such that legal remedies (separate suits) would be inadequate.
